beats.words: Education will no longer be the same due to AI.
beats.says: Education itself is about to change shape.
beats.picture: An open textbook is drawn on the axis, and a heart prints flat on its right page. On 'the same' that printed heart PEELS UP off the paper and settles above the book, leaving a dashed ghost of itself on the page it came off.
beats.whiteboard_version: The same drawing in marker: one open spread, the heart inked flat on the right page, then re-inked larger above the page while the first heart is left behind as a broken, dashed outline.

beats.words: Now, this guy on X built out an entire 3D interactive tool to be able to explore the entire human anatomy in a single afternoon, full of accurate 3D models.
beats.says: One developer shipped a whole interactive 3D anatomy tool in one afternoon.
beats.picture: The pointing cue lands first: the X post card by @thebuggeddev, with the marker highlight on the line that carries the claim, then a closer move into the screenshot the post carried (Anatomy Atelier, a 3D heart on screen). The card leaves and THE SAME HEART from beat 0 takes the stage large, gains three terracotta hotspot dots, sweeps once around a terracotta rotation arc on 'anatomy', and fills in its accurate interior vessels on 'accurate 3D models'.

emphasis.target: the claim line inside the X post card
emphasis.why: LAW 38 rule 1 - the words the viewer reads are type inside a raster post card, so the emphasis is the factory's marker fill, never a box and never a ring.

beats.whiteboard_version: The board cannot paste a raster, so the post is inked as a bordered card with a small X mark and the handle written, the claim line written inside it and the marker run under that line; then the card is erased and the heart is drawn big with its arc.

beats.words: No longer will we have to just look at textbooks and have to imagine things in our head.
beats.says: The old way was a flat page plus your imagination doing the rest.
beats.picture: Board clears. The textbook returns at the left, flat, and a boxed emphasis lands on it on 'textbooks'. At the right a head in profile is drawn, and inside its skull a heart is drawn with a line that never closes - the organ the reader is forced to invent.
objects: the imagined heart, dashed, inside the skull

emphasis.why: LAW 38 rule 2 - the target is a DRAWN object, not raster text, so it takes boxing (the DOM lane's panel border flip), never a ring or a highlight.

beats.whiteboard_version: Same two drawings side by side; the imagined heart is inked inside the head in dashes, and the emphasis is a marker box around the book rather than a border flip.

beats.words: Now we will be able to look at screens and see how things are built.
beats.says: Now you can open the thing up and look at how it is actually made.
beats.picture: Board clears. The heart returns centre stage and OPENS: its front half swings aside on a hinge at the notch, showing the chambers, the septum and the coronary lines inside, with a small cursor arrow resting where a hotspot was.
beats.whiteboard_version: The heart is drawn once, then its front half is erased and re-inked swung aside with the chambers drawn in behind it; INSIDE is written under it.

beats.words: Teachers who adopt AI will be able to build out interactive applications for all of their students.
beats.says: A teacher with AI can build one of these for her own class.
beats.picture: Board clears. Three real tool tiles sit in a row and send terracotta connectors down into a classroom easel; the heart appears on the easel's board on 'interactive applications' and the board's own border flips terracotta; then the model copies itself and the three copies land in a row on the easel's cross-brace - one for every student.

emphasis.why: LAW 38 rule 2 - the easel board is a DRAWN object, so the emphasis is the panel border flip; no ring, no ellipse, no circle.

beats.whiteboard_version: The tiles become three small inked marks in boxes, the easel is drawn legs first with its board propped on the ledge, and the three copies are three quick small hearts inked in a row on the brace.

beats.words: Now follow for more AI news, videos, and tutorials each and every single day, and catch you in the next one.
beats.picture: An opaque cream sheet rises and clears the board, then the chassis outro lockup fades up on this video's own themed object: the heart, drawn small, above the terracotta rule, the mono handle and the daily AI micro-line, all on one centred axis.
beats.whiteboard_version: Identical device - the rising sheet, then the same lockup on the same small heart.

bespoke_objects.name: open book heart
bespoke_objects.why_bespoke: The whole video is the flat printed page becoming a thing you can hold, and no stock mark says that. It is ONE two-part object - the open book AND the heart that has just left its page - declared with one bbox so the cold namer sees the whole idea rather than half of it.
bespoke_objects.how_drawn: Two ink-line page leaves meeting at a spine with a few ruled text lines on the left leaf, and above the right leaf a heart in the same ink with two vessel stubs, sitting clear of the page with a short lift line under it.

bespoke_objects.name: 3D anatomy heart
bespoke_objects.why_bespoke: The thing the developer actually built is a heart you can turn, and the source post's own screenshot opens on a heart - so the short's peak object is that heart, drawn in ink, with the rotation arc and hotspot dots that make it explorable rather than printed.
bespoke_objects.how_drawn: A heart silhouette in heavy ink with two great vessels at the top, a few interior vessel lines, three small terracotta hotspot dots on its face, and a terracotta arc with an arrowhead sweeping under it.

bespoke_objects.name: thinking head profile
bespoke_objects.why_bespoke: The old way's cost is invisible: the student has to build the organ in their own head. A head in profile with a dashed bubble holding a wobbly, unfinished heart is the only way to show guesswork as a picture.
bespoke_objects.how_drawn: A profile head outline (brow, nose, lips, chin, neck) in ink, with a dashed cloud growing off the crown that contains a small, deliberately wobbly heart drawn with a broken line.

bespoke_objects.name: classroom easel board
bespoke_objects.why_bespoke: The last beat moves from one developer to any teacher, and the teacher's own instrument is the board on its tripod. It carries the heart the class will use, which is what makes the beat a handover instead of a claim.
bespoke_objects.how_drawn: A rounded rectangle board on a ledge, standing on three splayed tripod legs with a cross-brace, all in ink line; the board's face stays empty until the heart is placed on it.

boards.why: LAW 43: chapters are the default and this script has five distinct idea groups, not one accumulating picture - the book becoming a thing, the developer's tool, the old way's cost, the inside of the model, the classroom. Holding all five on one surface at legible size is impossible on a phone, and nothing in beat 4 points back at the textbook drawing from beat 2.

chapters.why_together: the hook: one object, drawn complete, that carries the whole thesis.
the news and its evidence: the post that proves it and the object it produced.
the old way, stated as a pair: the flat page and the head that has to fill in the rest.
the new way, one picture: the same object opened up.
the handover to teachers: the tools, the board they build on, and the class that receives it.
